issues.legal_issue: The limitation period for a claim seeking a declaration of title begins when the defendant first clearly and unequivocally denies the asserted title.
material_facts: The original suit sought a permanent injunction and asserted ownership and possession of the property.
In the first written statement, the defendant denied the plaintiff’s title and asserted that the plaintiff had not established title to the property.
The plaintiff later amended the suit to add a claim for declaration of title, more than three years after that denial.
issues.conclusion: The right to sue for declaration first arose when the original written statement denied title. Because the declaration claim was added more than three years later, it was time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: Article 58 of the Limitation Act, 1963 provides a three-year period running from when the right to sue first accrues. As explained in Khatri Hotels Private Limited v. Union of India, a later or successive violation does not create a fresh period when the right to sue has already first accrued. The judgment relies on the principles in Bolo v. Koklan and Rukhmabai v. Lala Laxminarayan that a right to sue accrues upon an effective, clear and unequivocal threat to infringe the asserted right.

predicates.declaratory_title_claim: The claimant seeks a declaration of ownership or title to property.
predicates.defendant_first_unequivocally_denied_tit: The defendant clearly and unequivocally denied the claimant’s asserted title.
predicates.limitation_runs_from_first_denial: The limitation period for the declaratory claim is measured from the first clear denial of title.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks a declaration of title and the defendant has clearly denied that title, the limitation period is measured from that first denial.

issues.legal_issue: An amendment adding a claim that is already time-barred does not relate back to the filing of the original pleading when the court preserves the limitation defence and no special circumstances justify relation back.
material_facts: The original suit sought an injunction, and the later amendment added a declaration of title, introducing a claim for distinct relief.
The amendment was sought after the limitation period for the declaration claim had elapsed from the defendant’s original denial of title.
When allowing the amendment, the High Court expressly permitted the defendant to raise limitation.
The amendment did not involve the exceptional circumstances found in cases where no new material facts were needed and the amendment merely added an alternative legal claim.
issues.conclusion: The amendment did not relate back to the date the original suit was filed. The limitation defence remained available, and the declaration claim was time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits amendment of pleadings, but relation back is not universal and the court may direct that an amendment take effect from the date it was sought. Sampath Kumar v. Ayyakannu and Siddalingamma v. Mamtha Shenoy recognize that the doctrine may be displaced in an appropriate case. The general approach to amendments that would deprive a defendant of an accrued limitation defence is reflected in Pirgonda Hongonda Patil v. Kalgonda Shidgonda Patil, L.J. Leach & Co. Ltd. v. Jardine Skinner & Co., Vishwambhar v. Laxminarayan and Van Vibhag Karamchari Griha Nirman Sahkari Sanstha Maryadit v. Ramesh Chander. Exceptional circumstances may justify allowing an amendment despite limitation, but none were present here.

rule.if: civil_pleading_amendment and amendment_adds_time_barred_claim and court_preserves_limitation_defence and not exceptional_amendment_circumstances

predicates.civil_pleading_amendment: A party seeks to amend pleadings in a civil proceeding.
predicates.amendment_adds_time_barred_claim: The amendment adds a claim for which the limitation period has already elapsed.
predicates.court_preserves_limitation_defence: The court allows the amendment while expressly leaving the opposing party free to raise limitation.
predicates.exceptional_amendment_circumstances: Special circumstances exist that justify allowing the amendment despite the accrued limitation defence, such as the amendment adding no new material facts and merely supplying an alternative legal claim.
predicates.amendment_does_not_relate_back: The added claim is treated as brought when the amendment was sought, rather than when the original pleading was filed.

issues.definition: When a civil pleading amendment adds a time-barred claim, the limitation defence is preserved, and exceptional circumstances are absent, the added claim is treated as brought when the amendment was sought rather than when the original pleading was filed.
